reason: difficultez = difficultés, 'difficulties'; difficulrez is no word (t misread as r).
iugement = jugement, 'judgment', the word the sentence needs; ingement is no word (u misread as n). Same line as p135-b8l0-1, one choice of the line.
Bertrande is the name as Coras spells it everywhere; Berrrande is a misread of t as r.
ca|priuitate = captiuitate, the canon Coras cites again at annot-094 {d} as c. in captiuitate; ptiuitate is no word.
q or q. for quaestio: the abbreviation with or without its point; same citation (C. 34 q. 1).
D. de iur. dot. = de iure dotium, the Digest title, each word abbreviated with a point; a hyphen (iur-|dot.) would make one word of two abbreviations.
Ti|mothee = Timothée, the epistle cited (1 Timothy 5); motheo gives no French or Latin form of the name.
l'instabilité, 'instability', the noun paired with discretion and temerité; l'instabiliré is a misread of t as r.
c. tu absti|nes is the canon Si tu abstines (Augustine, De adulterinis coniugiis), cited by its incipit at annot-002 and again at {k} and {q} here; eu is no word.
The paragraph sign of this print is a swash capital P (conventions §2), as in l. j. P. fi. two words on; P. penul. = § penult.
l. iiij. and l. iij. of D. 48.4 both bear on aiding the enemy, so content cannot settle the numeral; the transcribers' first reading is kept and the uncertainty noted in the section Notes.
c. or c for capitulum: the siglum with or without its point; same citation.
Troas is Seneca's Troades, the sixth tragedy in the Renaissance order, where the line Coras paraphrases stands (Tro. 250, iuvenile vitium est regere non posse impetum); Tioas is no title.
ead. = eadem (causa et quaestione), the canon Si tu abstines in the same place as at {b}; and. is no abbreviation.

Reading B gives tout, the word the sense needs (tout le reste du monde); its point after seurs before & is a setting this print uses often mid-sentence. One choice of the whole line with p137-b0l16-2.
tout le reste du monde, 'all the rest of the world'; rout is no word (t misread as r). Same line as p137-b0l16-1.
incon|stãce and incon|stance are the same word inconstance, with or without the tilde for the n; no basis to see the tilde from the reflowed text, and the translation is the same.

P. fi. = § fin., the last paragraph, matching the same citation at {d} (l. j. P. fi. C. de assert. tollen.) which this note says was 'cited above'; P. si. would name a paragraph Si that the law does not want here.
cog|no. = cogno[vit], the Decretals title de eo qui cognovit consanguineam uxoris suae (X 4.13), as spelled out at annot-002 {l}; cog|gno. doubles the g.
Extrauagã[n]te = Extravagante, the constitution Ad reprimendum of Henry VII printed among the Extravagantes; Extraurgã- is no word.
reprimẽ-|dũ and reprimẽ|dũ are the same word reprimendum divided across margin lines, with or without the hyphen; same citation.
ib or ib. for ibi: the abbreviation with or without its point; same citation.
D. ad l. Iuli. maiesta. = Digest, Ad legem Iuliam maiestatis, the title's standard form, as at {e}, {t} and {u}; ed is no word.
laquelle, the relative; laquclle is a misread of e as c.
The clause runs on (tandis qu'elle l'ignore, & pense auoir affaire...); a comma suits the syntax. Translation the same either way.
xxxiij. or xxxiij before q. i.: the numeral with or without its point; same citation.
luy, the pronoun (du Tilh luy auoit donnees); lüy with a diaeresis is not a form this print uses.
The canons Si quis viduam and Si cuius (uxor adulterium commiserit) stand in Gratian's Distinctio 34, on the marriages of clerics; xxxiiij. is right and xxxiij. would misplace them.
col-|lation is the word collation divided across two margin lines; the hyphen is the expected sign of division. Same citation either way.
c. or c for capitulum before xx.: the siglum with or without its point; same citation (Genesis 20).
vn erreur, encore que la source d'iceluy n'aye bon fondement, excuse...: the subject and its concessive clause run on to the verb excuse, so a comma, not a point, after erreur.
Reading B gives toute (exempte de toute peine), the word the sense needs; colon or semicolon after publiquement is immaterial. One choice of the whole line with p140-b0l39-2.
toute peine, 'all punishment'; toate is no word (u misread as a). Same line as p140-b0l39-1.
The canon In lectum stands with Si virgo in Gratian's Causa 34 qq. 1-2 (the woman deceived by error of person), as the earlier reports record; xxxiiij. is right, xxxiij. would misplace it.
c. j. § quod autem, xxix. q. j. is Gratian's dictum on error of person, cited in just this form at annot-010 {h}; the numeral j. completes the citation, and the alternative is an unread sort.
c. Si virgo is in Causa 34 qq. 1-2 (as at p140-m0l1-1); xxxiiij. is right. The print's own xxxiij. at {d} on p138 is its error, not an alt.
iij. or iij before P.: the numeral with or without its point; same citation (D. 47.10.3).
c. or c for capitulum: the siglum with or without its point; same citation.
ij. or ij at the end of the note: the numeral with or without its point; same citation.
resou-|dre is the word resoudre divided at the line end; the hyphen is the expected sign of division. Sense unaffected.
manifester, 'to disclose' (manifester incontinent tel faict à son mari); manifelter is a misread of long s as l.
paßã and paſſã are the same word passam (l. Vim passam, D. 48.5.40), the double s set as ß or ſſ; same citation.
paßã and paſſã are the same word passam, as at p141-m3l0-1; same citation.
fœdißimã and fœdiſſimã are the same word foedissimam (C. 9.9.20), the double s set as ß or ſſ; same citation.
l. or l for lex, and D. or D: for Digestum: sigla with point or colon; same citation. One choice of the whole line with p141-m6l0-2.
D. or D: after P j.: the siglum's point or colon; same citation. Same line as p141-m6l0-1.
à, the preposition with its grave accent as this print sets it everywhere (appartient grandement à la dignité); â with a circumflex is not a form the print uses. Translation the same.
c. vt debitus. de appel. = the Decretals chapter Ut debitus honor under De appellationibus (X 2.28); c. is the siglum for a chapter, e. is no siglum.
D. deposit. = Digest, Depositi vel contra (D. 16.3), the title abbreviated with its vowel; depost. drops the i and is not a usual abbreviation of the title.
Heli, Heli, lam asabathani = Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani (Matthew 27:46) with the a of lama carried to the next word; reading A leaves the first letter unread.
soit entre vifs, ou à cause de mort: 'either inter vivos or mortis causa', the disjunctive ou; où ('where') makes no sense here.
entendues, the participle (ses conceptions & volontez soyent entendues); entendués is a stray accent.
con|sultiſſima and con|sultißima are the same word consultissima (C. 6.23.21, l. Hac consultissima), the double s set as ſſ or ß; same citation.
estre, the infinitive (pourroit estre trop curieusement recherché); estré is a stray accent.
de, the preposition (vne partie de la Gaule Belgique); dé is a stray accent.
Gaule, the noun (la Gaule fut iadis diuisee); Gaulé is a stray accent.
celle, the pronoun (appelee des Romains celle qui prenoit); cellé is a stray accent.
le, the article (par le fleuue de Garomne); lè is a stray accent.
picques, 'pikes', the weapon from which Coras derives the name Picards; pieques is no word (c misread as e).
